title: Two companies working together
description: Ledgerly, an accounting firm, is a PAP company to Ada's agent Atlas and a PAP personal agent at Northwind Bank for her. Every approval is Ada's. This is composition: draft 0.4 defines no company-to-company protocol.

parties.name: Ledgerly
parties.role: company to Atlas · personal agent at Northwind

steps.title: Atlas finds Ledgerly
steps.summary: To Atlas, Ledgerly is an ordinary PAP company: Atlas reads its protected resource metadata and poppy.json, and starts a signed-out, pairwise Session under a random sid, which sends no request.

chat.speaker: user
chat.text: Ledgerly keeps my books. Let it pay my Acme invoices from Northwind.

atlas.label: Session
atlas.value: signed out · a Session JWT on every request

atlas.label: Model sees
atlas.value: Summaries and statuses, never a credential

scopes.books:read: See your books: invoices, bills and payments
scopes.payments:write: Pay your bills, once you approve each payment

steps.title: Ada signs in to Ledgerly
steps.summary: Ada approves Atlas on Ledgerly's own page. Atlas's Session at Ledgerly now sends her access token.

steps.title: Ledgerly becomes a personal agent
steps.summary: To pay, Ledgerly needs Ada's Northwind account. It acts as a PAP personal agent with its own client_id and keys: it discovers Northwind, starts its own pairwise Session, and starts Device Sign-In there. Northwind verifies Ledgerly, not Atlas.

steps.title: Northwind returns the payment; Ledgerly relays it
steps.summary: Ledgerly finishes signing in at Northwind and asks Northwind's agent to pay. Northwind returns payments.transfer as an operation. Ledgerly cannot approve it for Ada, so it relays it to her as its own operation, quoting Northwind's summary as written.
